- L4 start Pat(46,28) = all b (6x6 solid b). Final = all O. So clicking (48,30) twice changed b→O. This is a "tile" that looks like a pattern (solid color). So the solid-color 6x6 blocks are also tiles (b/R/O tiles). At start, (46,28) was a b tile.
- L4 start Pat(38,28) = WWgggg/ggOOgg/WWWWWW — same as final. So the pattern at (38,28) didn't change during L4, and the level cleared with it still as a pattern! So the pattern is not something to be solved; it's static decoration/a clue!
So in L4: tiles (6x6 solid b/R/O) are clickable and cycle colors; patterns (mixed 3x3 cell blocks) are static clues. The level cleared when all tiles matched some target derived from the patterns.
Final L4 tiles:
Row 14: R O R b R
Row 22: R . R . R
Row 30: R O R R b
Row 38: . R . R .
Row 46: . O O R .
Static patterns:
P1 (22,20): g W g / g O g / g W g (center O)
P2 (22,36): g W g / g b g / g g W (center b)
P3 (38,28): W g g / W O g / W W W (center O)
P4 (46,28): was a b tile, clicked to O.
Wait, but P4 at start was a solid b tile, not a pattern. And it ended up as O. So that was just a tile.
So the L4 patterns are P1, P2, P3 (three static patterns). The final tile colors around them:
P1 (22,20) center O: neighbors: top (14,20)=O, bottom (30,20)=O, left (22,12)=R, right (22,28)=R.
P2 (22,36) center b: top (14,36)=b, bottom (30,36)=R, left (22,28)=R, right (22,44)=R.
P3 (38,28) center O: top (30,28)=R, bottom (46,28)=O, left (38,20)=R, right (38,36)=R.
Hmm. P1: vertical neighbors O, horizontal R. P2: top b, others R. P3: bottom O, others R.
Not consistent as "neighbors = center color."
New idea: maybe the pattern's cells encode the target colors of the 8 surrounding tiles, with W = "same as center" and g = "the other color" (i.e., not the center color). The center cell = the pattern's center color.
P1: center O. Cells: corners g, top W, bottom W.
Surrounding tiles: (14,12),(14,20),(14,28),(22,12),(22,28),(30,12),(30,20),(30,28).
Mapping (cell position → tile): top-left g→(14,12)=R; top W→(14,20)=O; top-right g→(14,28)=R; left g→(22,12)=R; right g→(22,28)=R; bottom-left g→(30,12)=R; bottom W→(30,20)=O; bottom-right g→(30,28)=R.
If W = center color (O): (14,20)=O ✓, (30,20)=O ✓. If g = "not center" → R ✓ (all 6 g cells → R).
P1 works!
P2 (22,36): center b. Cells: top-left g→(14,28)=R; top W→(14,36)=b ✓ (W=center b); top-right g→(14,44)=R; left g→(22,28)=R; right g→(22,44)=R; bottom-left g→(30,28)=R; bottom g→(30,36)=R; bottom-right W→(30,44)=b ✓ (W=center b).
P2 works! (All g → R, W → b.)
P3 (38,28): center O. Cells: top-left W→(30,20)=O ✓; top g→(30,28)=R ✓; top-right g→(30,36)=R ✓; left W→(38,20)=R ✗!!
Hmm, P3's left cell is W (should be O) but (38,20)=R. And bottom-left W→(46,20)=O ✓, bottom W→(46,28)=O ✓, bottom-right W→(46,36)=R ✗.
So P3: W cells: top-left, left, bottom-left, bottom, bottom-right. Corresponding tiles: (30,20)=O ✓, (38,20)=R ✗, (46,20)=O ✓, (46,28)=O ✓, (46,36)=R ✗.
Two mismatches. Hmm.
Unless the mapping isn't 1:1 positional. Maybe W = center color only applies to orthogonal cells, and g = other color only to diagonal cells? P3: orthogonal cells: top g→(30,28)=R ✓ (g=other), left W→(38,20)=R ✗ (W should be O).
Still fails.
Alternative: maybe the pattern indicates targets for tiles in a specific direction based on the pattern's "arrow" shape? P3's W cells: top-left, left, bottom-left, bottom, bottom-right — like a C-shape opening to the right. P1's W cells: top, bottom (vertical bar). P2's W cells: top, bottom-right.
Hmm, P1's W: top and bottom. The O tiles in P1's neighborhood: (14,20) top, (30,20) bottom. ✓ matches W positions.
P2's W: top, bottom-right. b tiles in P2's neighborhood: (14,36) top, (30,44) bottom-right. ✓ matches!
P3's W: top-left, left, bottom-left, bottom, bottom-right. O tiles in P3's neighborhood: (30,20) top-left, (46,20) bottom-left, (46,28) bottom. (38,20)=R left, (46,36)=R bottom-right. So W positions = {top-left, left, bottom-left, bottom, bottom-right} vs O positions = {top-left, bottom-left, bottom}. Mismatch: W has extra left and bottom-right.
Hmm, close but not exact. Unless (38,20) and (46,36) should have been O and I mis-solved L4? But the level cleared, so my final configuration was correct.
Wait — maybe I misread P3's cells. P3: WWgggg/ggOOgg/WWWWWW:
Row 1 (38): W W g g g g → cells (38,28)=W, (38,30)=g, (38,32)=g
Row 2 (40): g g O O g g → (40,28)=g, (40,30)=O, (40,32)=g
Row 3 (42): W W W W W W → (42,28)=W, (42,30)=W, (42,32)=W
So cells: top-left W, top g, top-right g; left g, center O, right g; bottom-left W, bottom W, bottom-right W.
I misread earlier! Left cell is g, not W. Redo: W cells: top-left, bottom-left, bottom, bottom-right. g cells: top, top-right, left, right.
Corresponding tiles: top-left (30,20)=O ✓; bottom-left (46,20)=O ✓; bottom (46,28)=O ✓; bottom-right (46,36)=R ✗.
Still one mismatch: bottom-right W → (46,36)=R.
Hmm. But wait — (46,36) is R and (46,28) is O. If W=center=O, then (46,36) should be O. But the level cleared with (46,36)=R.
Unless the pattern's bottom-right cell corresponds to a different tile… or the rule is "W cells indicate tiles that should be center color, but only if that tile exists / is within range"… (46,36) does exist.
Or maybe the rule is: g cells → other color (R), W cells → center color, but only for cells that are… hmm.
Let me re-verify the final L4 tile at (46,36). From the final tile map: row 46: ". O O R ." → (46,20)=O, (46,28)=O, (46,36)=R. Yes.
And (38,20)=R: P3's left cell g → other=R ✓.
So only (46,36) mismatches. Maybe the pattern only encodes 7 of the 8 neighbors (excluding bottom-right?), or the bottom-right W is a red herring.
Or maybe the rule is directional: the pattern encodes the neighbors in the direction the "W shape" points…
OK, I've spent enough time on L4. L5's patterns are different anyway (partial patterns inside tiles, M color, p color). L5's goal might be entirely different. Let me think about L5 from scratch.
L5 board:
- Tiles (6x6) at rows {4,12,20,28,36,44,52}, cols {6,14,22,30,38,46,54}.
- Tile colors: N (green) or G (dark gray).
- Full 3x3 cell patterns at tile positions: B(12,22), C(12,38), E(28,22), F(28,38), H(36,22), I(44,38).
- Partial patterns inside G tiles: A (bottom-right quadrant of (4,14)), D (right half of (28,6)), Gpat (left half of (28,54)), J (top-left quadrant of (52,46)).
- HUD: N at (0,54), p at (4,54).
Hypothesis: same as L4: patterns are static clues; tiles are clickable and cycle colors; goal = set each tile to its target color derived from patterns.
L5 tile colors: N and G. HUD shows N and p — hmm, p is purple. Maybe the tile cycle is N → p → G → N? Or the HUD shows the two "active" colors.
Wait, actually maybe the G tiles are just "gray" placeholders and the real colors are N and p (HUD). The G tiles might be "unset" tiles.
Pattern colors: N, M, W, g, p, G. If W/g are placeholders (as in L4), then literal colors in patterns: N, M, p, G.
Full patterns:
B(12,22): N M N / M N M / N M N — center N, M at edges.
C(12,38): W G G / g p G / W g W — center p.
E(28,22): N M N / M N M / N M N — center N.
F(28,38): g W g / W N W / g W g — center N.
H(36,22): W g W / g N g / W G W — center N.
I(44,38): N M N / M N M / N M N — center N.
Partial patterns:
A (bottom-right quadrant of tile (4,14)): N W / W g.
D (right half of tile (28,6)): g W / p g / g W.
Gpat (left half of tile (28,54)): g W / W N / g W.
J (top-left quadrant of tile (52,46)): g W / W N.
If the L4 rule (cell → surrounding tile, W=center color, g=other color) applies to full patterns:
B(12,22) center N, M cells: M is a new placeholder. If M = "other" and g = "other"… B: corners N, edges M. Surrounding tiles of (12,22): (4,14),(4,30),(12,14),(12,30),(20,14),(20,22),(20,30). Wait, (20,22) is a tile (row 20 has all 7 tiles). 8 neighbors: (4,14),(4,30),(12,14),(12,30),(20,14),(20,30) — only 6, since (20,22) is directly below… no wait, neighbors are 8 surrounding positions: rows 4,12,20 × cols 14,22,30 minus center (12,22): (4,14),(4,22)?, no.
Tile grid: rows R={4,12,20,28,36,44,52}, cols C={6,14,22,30,38,46,54}. Pattern B is at tile position (12,22) = grid (row 1, col 2). 8 neighbors: (0,1)=(4,14), (0,2)=(4,22)?? (4,22) is not a tile (row 4 tiles are only at 14, 22? no: row 4 tiles: (4,22),(4,30) — wait, from the 36px list: N 36 (4,22), N 36 (4,30). And G 20 (4,14) is a partial tile. So (4,14) is a tile (G), (4,22) is a tile (N), (4,30) is a tile (N).
B's neighbors: (4,14)=G, (4,22)=N, (4,30)=N, (12,14)=N, (12,30)=N, (20,14)=N, (20,22)=N, (20,30)=N.
B's cells: corners N (4), edges M (4). If N cell → target N, M cell → target "other" (G?):
(4,14)=N cell → target N. Currently G → click.
(4,30)=N → N ✓.
(12,14)=N → N ✓.
(12,30)=N → N ✓.
(4,22)=M → other=G? Currently N → click to G??
(20,14)=M → G? (20,22)=M → G? (20,30)=M → G?
Hmm, that would make many tiles G. Possible but let me check consistency with other patterns.
E(28,22) = same as B: N M N / M N M / N M N. Neighbors: (20,14)=N,(20,22)=N,(20,30)=N,(28,14)=N,(28,30)=N,(36,14)=N,(36,22)=N,(36,30)=N. All currently N.
If B and E have the same encoding, their neighbor targets are the same: corners N, edges G. B's corner neighbors: (4,14),(4,30),(12,14),(12,30) → N. Edge neighbors: (4,22),(20,14),(20,22),(20,30) → G.
E's corner neighbors: (20,14),(20,30),(36,14),(36,30) → N. Edge neighbors: (20,22),(28,14),(28,30),(36,22) → G.
Contradiction: (20,14) is a corner of B (→N) and an edge of E (→G). Contradiction!
So the L4 rule doesn't directly apply, or M is not "other."
Hmm. Unless the pattern's cells don't map to all 8 neighbors. Maybe only some cells are "active" (literal colors) and the rest are decorative.
Let me think about L5's patterns differently.
Look at F(28,38): g W g / W N W / g W g. This is exactly the L4 P1 style: corners g, edges W, center N. In L4, P1 (g W g / g O g / g W g) encoded: W cells (top, bottom) → center color O tiles; g cells (corners + left/right) → other color R.
So F: W cells (top, bottom) → N; g cells (corners, left, right) → other.
F's neighbors: (20,30),(20,38),(20,46),(28,30),(28,46),(36,30),(36,38),(36,46). All currently N.
If g → "other" = G: corners (20,30),(20,46),(36,30),(36,46) → G; left (28,30) → G; right (28,46) → G; top (20,38) → N; bottom (36,38) → N.
H(36,22): W g W / g N g / W G W. W cells: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right (corners!). g cells: top, left, right. G cell: bottom.
Hmm, H has a G (dark gray) cell at the bottom — literal G? If G is a literal target color: bottom neighbor (44,22) → G.
W cells → center N: corners (28,14),(28,30),(44,14),(44,30) → N. g cells → other=G: (28,22)?? Wait, H is at (36,22); neighbors: (28,14),(28,22),(28,30),(36,14),(36,30),(44,14),(44,22),(44,30).
Top cell g → (28,22) → G. But (28,22) is pattern E's position! No tile there. OK, ignore.
Left g → (36,14) → G. Right g → (36,30) → G.
Bottom G → (44,22) → G.
Corners W → (28,14),(28,30),(44,14),(44,30) → N.
C(12,38): W G G / g p G / W g W. Center p. W cells: top-left, bottom-left, bottom-right. G cells: top, top-right, right. g cells: left, bottom.
Neighbors of (12,38): (4,30),(4,38)?? Row 4 tiles: only 14, 22, 30. (4,38) doesn't exist. (4,46) doesn't exist either. So neighbors: (4,30) [top-left], (12,30) [left], (12,46) [right], (20,30) [bottom-left], (20,38) [bottom], (20,46) [bottom-right].
W → center p: (4,30)→p, (20,30)→p, (20,46)→p.
G → literal G?: (4,38) none, (12,46)→G, …
g → other: (12,30)→other, (20,38)→other.
Hmm, C's center is p — and the HUD shows p! So some tiles' target is p (purple). The W cells indicate p tiles: (4,30),(20,30),(20,46) → p.
But (4,30) is also a corner N cell of B → N. Contradiction again!
Ugh. (4,30): B says N (corner), C says p (W cell). Contradiction.
So the 8-neighbor mapping is wrong.
Let me step back and think about what else the patterns could mean.
Alternative: the pattern indicates the target color of the tile directly below/above it, or the pattern is a "key" that applies to a region.
Or: the pattern indicates the target of the tile it's on (in the case of partial patterns) — i.e., partial patterns on G tiles tell you what that tile should become:
A on (4,14): cells N W / W g. Literal: N. → target N?
J on (52,46): g W / W N. Literal: N. → target N.
D on (28,6): g W / p g / g W. Literal: p. → target p!
Gpat on (28,54): g W / W N / g W. Literal: N. → target N.
And full patterns at tile positions: the pattern itself is the "tile" and… in L4, patterns were static and the goal was about regular tiles. But in L5, maybe the full patterns are also clues for surrounding tiles.
Or in L5, the goal is: all tiles (including G ones) should be N, except where the pattern indicates p?
Hmm, what about the M cells in B/E/I? N M N / M N M / N M N. If M is a placeholder for "other"…
Let me try yet another interpretation: the pattern is a 3x3 preview of the tile's own target state — i.e., each tile (6x6 = 3x3 cells) should eventually become a 3x3 cell pattern matching the clue. The full pattern at a tile position is the target pattern for that tile (which is currently… missing? no, the pattern is there).
Wait — actually, in L5, the full patterns might be the tiles themselves (like L4's solid b tile at (46,28) that I clicked to O). In L4, solid tiles were clickable and cycled colors. In L5, maybe the pattern tiles are also clickable and cycle/transform, and the goal is to make them solid of the center color?
L4: (46,28) was solid b; I clicked twice → solid O. Was O the "correct" color? The level cleared after that. Maybe the goal was to make all tiles a specific color, or match the pattern.
Hmm, L4 had patterns P1, P2, P3 with centers O, b, O. And the final tiles were R/O/b mixed. The level cleared. I don't know the exact goal, but my final configuration cleared it.
Since I can't fully reverse-engineer L4's goal, let me probe L5 directly:
1. Click a plain N tile and see what changes (color cycle? N→p→G→N?).
2. Click a G tile with a partial pattern and see what happens.
3. Click a full pattern and see what happens.
Each probe = 1 action; the result will tell me the action model. Then I can infer the goal.
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider: maybe in L5, the goal is to make all tiles N (green), and the patterns indicate which tiles should instead be p (purple) or G (gray). The HUD shows N and p as the two "real" colors, and G is "wrong/unset."
Partial patterns on G tiles: A→N, J→N, D→p, Gpat→N. So the 4 G tiles' targets: (4,14)=N, (52,46)=N, (28,6)=p, (28,54)=N.
Full patterns: centers N (B, E, F, H, I) and p (C). If full patterns indicate the target of the tile at that position… but there's no tile at that position (the pattern occupies it). Unless the pattern is a tile that should become solid of the center color: B, E, F, H, I → solid N; C → solid p.
And plain N tiles stay N.
Goal: make the board all N, except (28,6)→p, C pattern→p, and the patterns become solid?
This is plausible: "paint the board green, purple where indicated."
How do clicks work? In L4, clicking a tile cycled its color (b→?→O after 2 clicks; b→R→O? or b→O→R? 2 clicks b→O). Tile colors in L4: b, R, O. Cycle might be b→R→O→b or b→O→R→b.
In L5, colors: N, G, p (and M?). Click cycle might be N→p→G→N or N→G→p→N.
Probe plan (3 actions, batched):
1. Click center of plain N tile (20,6) [tile (20,6), center (23,9)].
2. Click G tile (4,14) center (7,17).
3. Click full pattern B (12,22) center (15,25).
Then inspect the diff. Actually, to be safe, one at a time? Batching 3 different probes in one call is fine — the diff will show what each did (different regions).
Let me do that.
